verdict.rationale: First-party docs cover both modes in the story. An embedded database runs the same engine in-process with memory, disk, or object storage, exposed through a feature-gated embedded client in the Rust crate. The quickstart and `helix chef` start a local `dev` instance without any Cloud login. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of embedded mode; documentation of embedded support beyond the Rust crate (TypeScript, Go and Python appear HTTP-client only); explicit guidance on small-workload sizing for local instances.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the database embedded in-process or as a lightweight local instance for development and small workloads

citations.quote: Embedded database — run the same engine and queries in process with memory, disk, or object storage.
Initialize HelixDB, start a local instance, run the generated query, and stop it
`helix chef` can automate local scaffolding and agent setup without any Cloud login.
The same contract is available from a local server and a Helix Cloud gateway.
